## Description

## Summary

Adds `entire-agent-devin`, an Entire external agent (protocol v1, capabilities `hooks` + `transcript_analyzer` + `compact_transcript`) so Devin sessions become Entire sessions/checkpoints.

Devin exposes no transcript file, so the agent builds one from hook payloads:

```
Devin hook          -> entire hooks devin <name>  -> Entire event
SessionStart           session-start                SessionStart
UserPromptSubmit       user-prompt-submit           TurnStart (prompt, <received_chat_message> wrapper stripped)
PostToolUse            post-tool-use                none (transcript record only)
Stop                   stop                         TurnEnd -> checkpoint
PostCompaction         post-compaction              Compaction
SessionEnd             session-end                  SessionEnd (cloud Devin never fires it)
```

Every hook adds one JSONL `Record` to `.entire/tmp/devin/<session_id>.jsonl`. JSONL is required because Entire slices transcripts by line offset. The design rests on payloads captured from real Devin sessions (documented in `AGENT.md`):
- `tool_response`, and sometimes `tool_input`, arrive as Python-repr strings (`{'success': True, ...}`). `pyrepr.go` parses them into JSON.
- Payloads include no `cwd`, so repositories are located through `DEVIN_PROJECT_DIR`.
- The user-facing text is usually in `message_user` tool calls, not in `Stop.last_assistant_message`. Summaries and the compact transcript treat those calls as assistant text.
- The same hook can arrive twice: once from project hooks (`.devin/hooks.v1.json`, written by `install-hooks`) and once from the optional plugin in `plugin/`. A `<session>.seen` file stores `hook|prompt_id|tool_use_id|source` keys and drops the duplicate.

`entire-agent-devin dispatch --hook <name>` is not part of the protocol. The bundled Devin plugin calls it to forward a payload to `entire hooks devin <name>` in each repo whose Entire Devin hooks are installed. It checks the cwd, `$DEVIN_PROJECT_DIR`, and the `$ENTIRE_DEVIN_REPOS` globs (default `~/repos/*`). It always exits 0, so a failure here cannot break a Devin session.

`format-resume-command` returns `open https://app.devin.ai/sessions/<id>`, because Devin has no CLI resume.

## Blueprint authoring guide

Sections:
- `initialize`: Commands that run once when the snapshot is first built (e.g., installing tools, global dependencies). Only filesystem changes persist — running processes (Docker containers, background services) will NOT be running when the snapshot boots. Do not start services here. Commands should be idempotent.
- `maintenance`: Commands that run during snapshot builds to keep dependencies up to date (e.g., npm install, pip install). At session start, these are surfaced to the agent as context — NOT auto-executed. Only include dependency installation commands — avoid build commands (e.g., `npm run build`, `make`, `cargo build`) unless the user explicitly asks. Must be fast and incremental — do NOT use commands that wipe and reinstall (e.g., `npm ci`, `rm -rf node_modules && npm install`); use incremental equivalents (e.g., `npm install`).
- `knowledge` (optional): Named entries with `name` and `contents` fields. Keep `contents` to short commands or one-liners. Boilerplate includes `lint`, `test`, `startup` — only populate ones you discovered. Free-form, but prefer boilerplate fields plus `notes` if the user asks for more detail.

Do not put the same command in both `initialize` and `maintenance`.

By default, `initialize` and `maintenance` take a multi-line string. For per-step names, use the expanded list form:
```yaml
initialize:
  - name: install uv
    run: curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh
  - run: npm install
```

To set environment variables for subsequent steps, write KEY=VALUE lines to $ENVRC (like GitHub Actions' $GITHUB_ENV). For example:
```yaml
initialize: |
  echo "NODE_ENV=production" >> $ENVRC
```

Commands run from the repo root. Use subshells for subdirs: `(cd subdir && command)`.

## Platforms (`runs-on`)

Each YAML document in a blueprint is a block that builds on one platform, selected by its top-level `runs-on:` key (e.g. `runs-on: macos`, `runs-on: windows`). A block without `runs-on` is the default Linux block and is only ever built on Linux — setup for any other platform silently never runs. So when the commands you verified ran on a non-Linux machine, the block containing them MUST start with the matching `runs-on:`; never put non-Linux commands in the default block. A blueprint can hold several blocks separated by `---`, each declaring a different platform, and each block has its own `initialize`/`maintenance`/`knowledge` sections — to add a platform to an existing blueprint, append a new `---`-separated block rather than editing the default one:
```yaml

  npm install
---

initialize: |
```
